title: Glacier Melt, Sea-Level Rise and the Changing Arctic

cards.h: Syllabus theme: changes in critical geographical features
cards.b: The GS1 syllabus asks about 'changes in critical geographical features (including water bodies and ice-caps) and in flora and fauna, and the effects of such changes'. This lesson gives the ice, the sea and the Arctic in one place with data and examples.

About 99 percent of glacial ice sits in the Antarctic and Greenland ice sheets. Antarctica alone holds about 58 m of potential sea-level rise, Greenland about 7 m. Mountain glaciers hold far less (about 0.3 m) but supply rivers to billions. Sea ice floats, so melting it does not raise sea level much, but loses its reflecting effect.

Arctic amplification: the Arctic is warming nearly four times as fast as the world average since 1979, according to a 2022 study. Reasons: ice-albedo feedback (dark water absorbs more heat), more heat from the oceans, and changes in clouds and the atmosphere. Summer Arctic sea ice has fallen about 12-13 percent a decade since 1979.

Global mean sea level has risen about 20-25 cm since 1900 and the rate is now over 4 mm a year. Causes: thermal expansion of warming water and melt of ice sheets and glaciers. The IPCC AR6 (2021) projects about 0.28-1.01 m by 2100 depending on emissions, with higher values possible if ice sheets collapse. Low islands (Tuvalu, Maldives, Kiribati) and deltas are most at risk.

Thresholds beyond which change is hard to reverse: loss of the Greenland ice sheet, collapse of the West Antarctic ice sheet (Thwaites, the 'Doomsday Glacier'), thawing permafrost releasing methane, and weakening of the AMOC (Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation), which warms Europe. Scientists such as Timothy Lenton have mapped these 'tipping elements'.

About a quarter of the northern hemisphere land is permafrost. Thaw releases CO2 and methane, damages roads and buildings in Siberia and Alaska, and creates thermokarst lakes and sinkholes (the Batagaika crater in Siberia). The Siberian heatwave in 2020 reached 38 degrees C in Verkhoyansk.

New routes: the Northern Sea Route along Russia and the Northwest Passage through Canada save thousands of km between Asia and Europe. Resource claims on oil and gas. The Arctic Council (1996) has eight members; India got observer status in 2013 and set up Himadri station at Ny-Alesund (2008), Svalbard. India's Arctic Policy came in 2022.

The Antarctic Treaty (1959) bans military use and mining; the Madrid Protocol (1991) protects the environment. West Antarctica loses ice, while parts of East Antarctica have gained snow at times. India has stations Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012) and a new Antarctic Act (2022) to regulate activity there. Antarctic sea ice hit record lows in 2023.

India has about 7,500 km of coast with the Sundarbans, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai and the Maldives-like Lakshadweep at risk. Sea-level rise is about 3.3 mm a year in India's north Indian Ocean. Himalayan glacier retreat endangers river flow, with GLOF hazards. Responses include the CRZ rules, cyclone shelters, and mangrove restoration.

Likely questions: 'Melting of polar ice and its impact on India', 'Arctic opening: opportunities and risks', 'Tipping points in the climate system'.

  • Cause: warming, albedo feedback. Effect: sea level, circulation, weather.
  • Give India: coast, monsoon, Himalayan rivers and polar stations.
  • Finish with mitigation and adaptation plus treaties.
